thread:
Elaine (AE): Quick sync on Mosaic POC — buyer expects ~500 qps sustained, target p99 < 150ms. Need a scheduled run tomorrow 09:00 PT. Who can own infra/setup?
Devon (SE): I can run it. Plan: 30m ramp, two 5m burst windows at peak. We'll use a staging pool with prefix cache enabled.
Priya (Eng): Heads up — enabling KV prefix cache should cut per-token compute ~25-35% on this workload. Baseline model: redwood/gpt-small-quant-v2 (same as the prospect asked).
Nina (SRE): Security check: they asked if SOC2 + customer KMS required for PII. Short answer: for PII we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS; Dedicated is fine for non-PII. I'll prepare the exact questionnaire wording.
Elaine (AE): Pricing Q from procurement: what does sustained 500 qps mean for committed capacity costs vs hosted? Need a ballpark to include in the SOW.
Devon (SE): Back-of-envelope calc: assume avg 25 tokens in + 75 tokens out = 100 tokens per request. 500 qps * 3600s = 1.8M requests/hr -> 180M tokens/hr. At hosted rate $0.00003/token that's ~$5,400/hr. With Dedicated reserved capacity the unit cost drops a lot; I'll draft a committed pricing option.
Elaine (AE): Please add that as a line-item in the proposal draft — buyer wants monthly and annual commit examples.
Devon (SE): Will do. Quick copy of the load command we used in staging:
```bash
wrk -t12 -c1000 -d600s -s scripts/llm_post.lua --latency http://staging.redwood/api/generate
```
Devon (SE): Summary from the last run (staging, prewarm off): avg 135ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms, errors 0.2% (most 429s during bursts).
Priya (Eng): The p99 spike aligns with KV cache misses and cold wasm kernels. If we prewarm KV and warm kernels, p99 drops to ~230ms in our tests. Recommend adding a prewarm step to the runbook.
Nina (SRE): For the security questionnaire entry on encryption-at-rest, use our standard Dedicated answer: "Customer-managed keys via cloud KMS/HSM supported; audit logs available; retention 90 days." I'll DM the exact copy.
Elaine (AE): Buyer also asked about cross-region failover during a heavy load — can we simulate that?
Priya (Eng): Yes, we can script a region-failover during the second burst window and measure tail latency. We'll highlight the fallback behavior in the demo.
Elaine (AE): Next actions: (1) Devon runs 45m test tomorrow 09:00 PT with KV prewarm + region failover; (2) Priya adds prewarm script to repo; (3) Nina prepares KMS/security snippet; (4) Elaine updates SOW with Hosted vs Dedicated monthly commit examples + the rough $/hr calc.
Devon (SE): ack. I'll post raw results & latency histograms here after the run and include p50/p95/p99 + error classes. Tagging the buyer channel: <https://mosaic.example.com/buyer-thread|mosaic-buyers>.
